text.p: Arsenal's hopes of snatching England's second European Champions' League spot were dented by relegation strugglers Coventry when they were held to a 1-1 premier league away draw on Monday.
It left Arsenal in second place on 65 points but only one point ahead of Liverpool, who have a game in hand, and four points behind leaders Manchester United who have played two matches fewer.
A series of missed chances, especially by striker Ian Wright in the second half, effectively ended Arsenal's faint hopes of overhauling the league leaders.
Only a mistake by Coventry goalkeeper Steve Ogrizovic which enabled Wright to hit a first half equaliser gave the London club a point.
Coventry, looking far better than their lowly position suggests, took the lead in the second minute when Dion Dublin drove the ball past England goalkeeper David Seaman.

Arsenal pressed for the equaliser and although they wasted several chances they were finally rewarded in the 20th minute when Ogrizovic brought down Wright in the penalty area after failing to hold on to a soft shot from Paul Merson.
Wright sent Ogrizovic the wrong way from the ensuing penalty to level the scores. Arsenal pressed hard for much of the remainder of the match but Coventry held firm.
It left them on 38 points from 36 matches but with all the five teams below them with matches in hand.
